concepts.title: Physical Divisions of India
concepts.definition: India's land falls into broad physical divisions: the Himalayas in the north, the northern plains watered by great rivers, the peninsular plateau, the deserts, the coastal strips and the island groups.
concepts.key_idea: Each division has its own land, climate and life, and together they make India's geography rich and distinct.

concepts.title: Rivers of India
concepts.definition: Great rivers give India its shape of life: the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra flow from the Himalayas, while the Narmada, Tapi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri drain the peninsula.
concepts.key_idea: Rivers water the fields, carry trade and draw pilgrims, so civilisations bloom along their banks.

concepts.title: Reading the Physical Map of India
concepts.definition: A physical map shows mountains, plateaus, plains, rivers and seas through colour and signs; reading it lets you trace journeys from the peaks to the islands and see how the land rises and falls.
concepts.key_idea: Maps turn a whole subcontinent into one page you can read at a glance.

concepts.title: Diversity and the Character of the Land
concepts.definition: The chapter opens with the thought that India's very geography gives it a national character; from Himalayan snow to Kanyakumari's seas, the varied land is one home whose diversity knits the people together.
concepts.key_idea: Geographical diversity is not a barrier but a bond: different lands, one country.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why do the Himalayas matter to the whole of India?

solution_template.explain: The Himalayas wall the subcontinent and give birth to its great rivers.
Those rivers spread fertile plains where most Indians farm and live, so the mountains feed the nation.
